10.1002_adma.74007: Aqueous zinc‐iodine batteries (AZIBs) are promising candidates for flexible electronics owing to their intrinsic safety. Nevertheless, their practical deployment is impeded by severe interfacial challenges, including polyiodide shuttling, zinc (Zn) dendrite growth, and parasitic reactions. Herein, a Zn 2 + ‐induced molecular self‐assembly strategy based on natural glycyrrhizic acid (Gl) is proposed to construct a robust dual‐network hydrogel electrolyte. The self‐assembled Gl nanofibrous network can simultaneously and effectively regulate the dual electrode/electrolyte interfaces. At the anode interface, the Gl nanofibrous network adsorbed on the Zn surface enables homoepitaxial Zn plating, promoting uniform Zn nucleation and growth. At the cathode interface, the p – π conjugated structure and nanofibrous network of Gl cooperatively immobilize polyiodides, effectively suppressing the shuttle effect. Consequently, the Zn||Zn symmetric cell exhibits excellent cycling stability over 1900 h at 1 mA cm −2 with 1 mAh cm −2 . The Zn||I 2 pouch cell achieves a long lifespan with a high‐capacity retention of 78.1% and a low N/P ratio of 1.93. Moreover, leveraging the high biocompatibility and flexibility of this self‐assembled hydrogel, an on‐body transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) device integrated with the Zn||I 2 battery delivers a stable 1.5 mA current for therapeutic neuromodulation, demonstrating a feasible pathway for flexible on‐body AZIBs.
10.1002_advs.202508646: Aqueous zinc–bromine batteries (ZBBs) are promising candidates for renewable energy storage, offering advantages over lithium‐ion batteries. However, their widespread adoption is hindered by challenges such as zinc dendrite formation and water decomposition, which lead to short circuits, electrode degradation and reduced cycle life. Therefore, this study presents a facile strategy for in‐situ construction of a fluorinated solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) formed via coating graphite current collectors with a lubricant hydrophobic perfluoropolyether interlayer. During the initial charging process, a fluoride‐rich SEI layer forms to regulate Zn nucleation and suppress dendrite growth. This SEI promotes uniform zinc deposition and inhibits hydrogen evolution by limiting water access to the electrode surface, thereby enhancing cycle life and energy efficiency. As a result, ZBBs incorporating this SEI exhibit a substantial reduction in potential hysteresis from 285 to 60 mV, deliver an energy density of nearly 20 Wh L −1 and an areal capacity of 10.7 mAh cm −2 , and maintain >79% energy efficiency over 1000 cycles. This work offers a scalable approach to achieving high‐performance ZBBs, advancing the development of next‐generation anode‐free zinc batteries.
10.1002_aenm.202504829: Aprotic lithium‐oxygen (Li‐O 2 ) batteries are considered promising next‐generation energy storage systems because of their high energy density, but their practical application is hindered by their limited discharge capacity. Water is regarded as significantly enhancing discharge capacity, but its effect on solvation and interfacial behavior is not fully understood. Herein, combined with molecular dynamics simulations, electron microscopy, and electrochemical analyses, it is elucidated that water‐driven solvation structure reconstruction dictates lithium peroxide (Li 2 O 2 ) nucleation behavior and enables crossover electrochemistry that governs Li anode corrosion. Specifically, moderate water introduction promotes Li 2 O 2 growth at the grooves of pre‐formed Li 2 O 2 deposits, expanding limited active sites on the cathode, thereby breaking the capacity ceiling. Furthermore, it is confirmed that Li anode corrosion, a controllable electrochemical reaction rather than chemical diffusion, is governed by cathode‐induced crossover electrochemistry. This previously overlooked coupling is initiated by water‐modulated solvation structures, effectively enhancing species mass transport while suppressing anode corrosion. This work provides fundamental insights into water‐mediated electrochemical processes and offers strategic guidance for optimizing Li‐O 2 batteries.
10.1002_smll.76523: Room‐temperature sodium‐sulfur (RT‐Na/S) batteries have been recognized as promising next‐generation batteries with high energy density and low material price, but their practical implementation is severely obstructed by fatal safety issues owing to the direct application of Na metal. To address this concern, sodium sulfide (Na 2 S) has been emerging as a promising cathode material which could enable the utilization of sodium‐free anodes whilst additionally mitigating the volume expansion of S. However, Na 2 S‐based RT‐Na/S batteries are still in their infancy, facing significant challenges related to a high activation energy barrier required to convert Na 2 S to polysulfides during the initial charge and sluggish reaction kinetics for sulfur species. In this review, the three most promising types of Na 2 S‐based sodium‐free RT‐Na/S full‐cells are first comprehensively discussed to establish the strengths and obstacles being researched for each system. Subsequently, the working mechanism and inherent advantages and weaknesses of Na 2 S are methodically detailed. Utilizing this knowledge, strategies to enhance its performance are reviewed from three perspectives: synthesis methods, structural regulation, and catalytic optimization. Finally, this review summarizes these developments and offers an outlook of future research directions into developing superior Na 2 S‐based cathodes toward safer and high‐energy Na 2 S‐based sodium‐free RT‐Na/S batteries.
10.1016_j.ijheatmasstransfer.2026.128991: The efficient operation of PEM fuel cells requires humidifying the supply air. This can be achieved by integrating a membrane humidifier into the cathode subsystem. In this paper, a second law analysis of a flat membrane humidifier is carried out using a detailed dynamic simulation model that is discretized along the channel. The newly developed modeling and analysis approach enables a detailed calculation of entropy production in membrane humidifiers under steady state and transient operating conditions. Suitable equations are introduced and implemented to model the entropy production rates inside the humidifier due to mass and heat transfer as well as friction. With the model, inevitable entropy production due to water transfer can be distinguished from entropy production by heat and momentum transfer. The model is verified and validated using literature data. In addition, the effect of discretization on accuracy and calculation speed of our model are discussed. It is found that the model is accurate and offers fast calculation times. With the model, the effects of geometry and operating conditions are analyzed by simulation. It is found that water transfers in the membrane and the dry side channels are the dominant entropy production mechanisms in most conditions and geometries investigated. In an analyzed start-up procedure starting from ambient temperature it is found that entropy production caused by each mechanism dominates at some point in time. Finally, a new analytic approach based on the mass transfer efficiency is proposed that allows to calculate the entropy production caused by water transfer in a balanced counterflow humidifier using inlet quantities and the mass transfer efficiency. • A new model is proposed to calculate entropy production in membrane humidifiers. • Entropy production by heat, mass and momentum transfer are considered in the model. • For water transfer, a new relation of efficiency and entropy production is found. • Water transfer is found to be the dominant source of entropy production. • The effect of geometry on individual entropy production mechanism is investigated.
10.1016_j.jia.2026.10.003: In this study, silver nanoparticles (Ag-NPs) were evaluated as a multifunctional nanotechnological material for mitigating stress induced by microplastics (MPs), a persistent form of biological contaminant, and fungal pathogens ( Colletotrichum brevisporum causing anthracnose and Fusarium oxysporum causing root rot) within a soybean. Ag-NPs exhibited strong antifungal activity, suppressing mycelial growth of C. brevisporum by 73% at 90 μg mL −1 and F. oxysporum by 56% at 60 μg mL −1 , resulting in reduced disease incidence of 54% and 61%, respectively, and improved photosynthetic performance. Beyond direct pathogen inhibition, Ag-NPs activated nanoscale defense responses by enhancing antioxidant enzyme activities, inducing defense-related gene expression, and promoting callose deposition, thereby alleviating oxidative stress as evidenced by reduced malondialdehyde and hydrogen peroxide levels. Ag-NPs treatment also improved seed germination and root biomass, counteracting the detrimental effects of combined MP and pathogen stress. Importantly, Ag-NPs significantly reduced heavy metal accumulation in soil, roots, and leaves, whereas MP exposure alone or in combination with fungal infection markedly increased heavy metal uptake in soybean. While fungal infection alone had minimal influence on metal accumulation, MPs substantially exacerbated heavy metal toxicity within the soybean. Overall, the present study demonstrates that Ag-NPs function as a dual-purpose nanomaterial capable of simultaneously suppressing phytopathogens and mitigating biological contaminant-associated metal stress. These findings provide mechanistic insight into nano-enabled environmental protection and highlight the potential of Ag-NPs as a materials-based strategy for enhancing resilience in contaminated plant-soil systems which have soybean crops.
10.1021_acs.analchem.6c04234: Nanoplastics represent an emerging contaminant of growing environmental and public health concern, with polyethylene terephthalate (PET) being on topic due to its dominant use in beverage packaging. This study presents a SERS approach for the detection and quantification of PET nanoplastics in commercial bottled water, combining SERS with colloidal silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) and commercial solid SERS substrates, with automated Pearson correlation spectral classification. Mapping SERS samples of PET-bottled water combined with a Python identification algorithm enabled the detection of PET nanoplastics, while SEM-EDX analysis confirmed the presence of nanoscale carbon-oxygen particles consistent with PET stoichiometry. Beyond PET, phthalocyanine pigment nanoparticles, likely originating from bottle package, and inorganic residues including calcite, gypsum, and sodium nitrate were simultaneously identified, demonstrating the multianalyte capability of the approach. Using colloidal AgNPs, the estimated PET nanoplastic concentration was 17.25 ± 1.6 million particles per 0.5 L bottle (34.5 ± 3.2 million particles/L), comparative with values reported by nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA) and stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy in comparable studies. The method requires minimal sample preparation, limited to concentration by evaporation, without digestion or extraction steps, and preliminary results can be obtained within a few hours. These findings establish SERS combined with automated spectral analysis as a practical and sensitive screening tool for nanoplastic monitoring in drinking water, reporting particle concentrations directly in the number of particles per liter and with potential applicability to broader water quality analysis.
10.1186_s13065-026-01740-1: To effectively treat refractory azo dye wastewater, microwave advanced catalytic oxidation technology was adopted to degrade the model pollutant methyl orange using activated carbon fiber (ACF)/CuO as the catalyst and potassium persulfate (K 2 S 2 O 8 ) as the oxidant. The optimized experimental parameters and the degradation pathway of methyl orange were determined. The results showed that when the microwave power was 500 W, the irradiation time was 2 min, the dosage of potassium persulfate was 0.6 g/L, and the dosage of ACF/CuO was 10 g/L, the removal rate of methyl orange solution was close to 100%, the COD removal rate was 89.65%, and the TOC removal rate was 72.36%. Mechanism analysis indicated that the double bond was broken to generate acid and p -nitrophenol, which were gradually degraded to benzene and phenol under the oxidation of sulfate radical. Subsequently, the benzene and phenol underwent chain cleavage to form maleic anhydride, and part of the benzene, phenol, and the generated maleic anhydride were ultimately degraded to water and carbon dioxide.
